clue.text: Built-up city band is pissed, without energy

indicators.note: a drunk person is scrambled and unsteady, so the letters lose their order
in its old sense 'without' means outside, so one piece sits on the outside of another

blocks.note: Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, a crossword favourite
taken as written, to be rearranged
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A town's band has drunk itself into exhaustion.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged band-letters split around the energy symbol, with the city tacked on in front: UR + BANIS(E)D.
explanation.definitionFit: An area that has been built up has turned from countryside into town, which is exactly what urbanised describes.

clue.text: Pissed off over sex initiated with alien

indicators.note: something initiated is only begun, so just its opening letter is used

blocks.note: when time is over, it is up
the opening letter of the word
ET is the film's extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: Someone is cross about a sexual encounter with an alien.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pissed off' is British slang for annoyed, not drunk; 'over' gives UP as in 'your time is up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being annoyed and being distressed are close synonyms in everyday British speech, both describing a bad mood.

clue.text: Flier guards source of lie about Brown? Glaringly obvious

the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A bird shields a lie told about Gordon Brown, the former Labour prime minister, and the deceit is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown suggests Gordon Brown, the UK prime minister, but it is just a colour; 'about' rearranges it rather than reversing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something blatant is done openly and shamelessly, so it is plain for everyone to see.

clue.text: Prick's end tickled with eel

indicators.note: being tickled makes you squirm about, so the letters wriggle into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A smutty image of a man's member being teased by a slippery fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prick's end' reads as one phrase, but the 's is 'is' and joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To prick something is to pierce it with a sharp point, and a pin or sewing tool does exactly that, so either verb works.

clue.text: Crafty thing secures drug ring in club

indicators.note: something placed in another thing is enclosed by it

blocks.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A cunning operator gets hold of a drug-dealing gang in a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crafty' looks like cunning, but a craft is a boat, so a 'crafty thing' is a kind of vessel. SPEED + B(O)AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat is a watercraft, so the setter jokes that a fast motor vessel is a thing belonging to the craft family.

clue.text: Is Conservative leader at the heart of party music venue?

the first letter of the word

explanation.walkthrough: Everything placed inside the party: D(IS C)O.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a club or event where people dance to recorded pop music, so it counts as a place for music.

clue.text: Bashes – they come in twos

blocks.note: first meaning: punches or hits hard, as a verb
second meaning: garments for the feet, sold and worn in pairs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bashes' can be a noun meaning parties, but here it is the verb to hit; the second definition is a cryptic description of footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: To sock someone is slang for punching them, and the foot garments are always bought as a matching pair.

clue.text: Brenda, out of underwear straps, is a swinger

indicators.note: something taken out of a word is removed from it, leaving the rest

blocks.note: suspenders are straps holding up stockings

explanation.surface: The Queen escapes her stocking straps and turns out to be a swinger.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye, where Cyclops sets, calls the late Queen 'Brenda'; her initials ER come out of the middle of the straps.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to hang it, and anything hanging can swing, so the verb phrase means dangles.

clue.text: Extreme Right Tory sources protected by killer, for sure

indicators.note: a source is where something begins, so each word gives its first letter
a protector surrounds what it keeps safe, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
the opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Hard-right Conservative informants are being shielded by an assassin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extreme' looks like a political adjective but is just one of three words supplying first letters: C(ERT)AIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is so 'for sure' means you have no doubt about it, which is what being sure or definite means.

clue.text: Who'll save the world from the woman embraced by obnoxious poseur?

an embrace wraps arms around someone, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the pronoun for a woman

explanation.walkthrough: 'Obnoxious' reads as an insult to the poseur, but it is the signal to rearrange that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic-book champions like Superman are forever rescuing the planet from destruction, so the question describes them.

clue.text: Flagrant imitation gets E-

blocks.note: a sham is a fake or imitation
the minus sign after E is read as 'E less'

explanation.surface: A blatant copy earns only an E-minus grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E-' looks like a poor school mark, E minus, but read the minus as 'less' and you have E then LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant behaviour is brazen and done without any embarrassment, so it shows no sense of guilt.

clue.text: Whip rejected members

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown back, so the letters go back to front

blocks.note: parts are members or components of a whole

explanation.surface: A party whip turns away MPs from the party.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a parliamentary whip, the official who keeps MPs in line, and its members; here whip is a verb or a lash.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap is a leather band used to beat someone, and to strap a person is to flog them.

clue.text: Scoffed after Tory leader held up rear

indicators.note: one thing after another places it second in the line
a leader goes in front, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
to rail is to scoff at or protest bitterly

explanation.surface: People jeered after the Conservative leader was delayed at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held up' looks like 'delayed', but 'held up rear' means came last; scoffed means mocked, not ate greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up the rear in a race or procession is to lag behind everyone, which is what trailing means.

clue.text: Outside, making love, dash off with wind

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
to dash off a letter is to pen it quickly
wind is moving air

explanation.surface: Having sex outdoors, then leaving hurriedly with flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making love' tempts you towards sex, but love is the tennis nought, and 'dash off' means write hurriedly, not run.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held outdoors, like a concert or theatre, takes place under the sky rather than in a building.

clue.text: (& 19ac./14ac.) Dodgy convenience food of Tory leader? It could be the end of him

definitions.text: It could be the end of him

indicators.note: something dodgy is unsound and not to be trusted, so the letters are reworked
a leader goes in front, so the first letter is taken

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A party leader's dubious ready meal might finish him off.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'end of him' looks like food poisoning, but 'him' is the Tory leader and the danger is political.
explanation.definitionFit: When MPs pass such a motion against a prime minister or party leader, it usually forces him from office.

clue.text: Lobby representative, finally, but lives will be ruined

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so the last letter is kept
something ruined is wrecked, so its letters are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: the last letter of the word
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lobbyist's work will go through in the end, but people's lives will be wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lobby' and 'representative' together suggest political lobbying; the definition is the entrance hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobby is the entrance hall of a building, and a vestibule is a small hall just inside the front door.

clue.text: see 13ac.
Infallible buffoon wants Pence topping?

blocks.note: a buffoon is a fool
p is the abbreviation for pence
a roof is the topping of a house

explanation.surface: A clown who thinks himself never wrong wants Mike Pence, Trump's vice-president, killed off.
explanation.walkthrough: Pence is Mike Pence, but here it is the coin plural abbreviated to p; 'topping' is a roof, not an execution.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan or device that cannot go wrong, even when mishandled by an idiot, is reliable and therefore infallible.

clue.text: Use bugging device and experience too much audio input?

blocks.note: first meaning: to listen in on talk not meant for you
second meaning, split cryptically: an excess plus taking in sound

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is playful: 'too much' is OVER and 'experience audio input' is HEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Listening covertly to conversations through a hidden microphone is a way of eavesdropping on private talk.

clue.text: Slavering Cyclops taking part in rescue

indicators.note: to take part in something is to be inside it, so one piece is put within another

blocks.note: salvation is rescue or deliverance
the setter Cyclops refers to himself, as I

explanation.surface: The drooling one-eyed giant joins a rescue mission.
explanation.walkthrough: Cyclops is this puzzle's setter, so his name stands for I, as 'setter' or 'yours truly' does elsewhere: SAL(I)VATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavering is letting spit dribble from the mouth, and the noun for producing spit is used for that drooling.

clue.text: Being narrow, acted like many a politician, holding back time virtually

definitions.note: the clue's '-ing' phrase works as an adjective, as the answer does

indicators.note: virtually means almost, so the word is cut short of its final letter
going back means travelling in the other direction, so the letters run backwards
to hold something is to grip it on both sides, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: the satirical view that politicians tell lies
taken as written, then shortened and turned round

explanation.surface: A narrow-minded politician lied, practically turning back the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virtually' means almost, so the word is cut short by a letter before it is turned round; three operations stack on one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something narrow in scope or outlook is restricted, so being narrow is being confined within bounds.

the first letter of the word

clue.text: Liberal on the inside, Morgan is a tool!

explanation.definitionFit: Pliers are a hand-held gripping instrument with two jaws, found in any workshop toolbox.

clue.text: Claim Merseyside has swallowed Bury?

explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a real town in Greater Manchester, so it looks like a proper noun; it is the verb to bury.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury something in work or water is to sink it completely, which is what immerse means.

clue.text: Tip removed from contraceptive by ghastly, devoted traveller

clue.text: Joint head of trust in the shit

clue.text: Lefty lies about his material situation and things he likes to do?

definitions.text: his material situation and things he likes to do
